etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English liklihode, equivalent to likely +‎ -hood.

definitions.definition: The probability of a specified outcome; the chance of something happening; probability; the state or degree of being probable.
(statistics, probability theory) The probability that some fixed outcome was generated by a random distribution with a specific parameter.

quote.citation: 1614, Walter Ralegh [i.e., Walter Raleigh], chapter 3, in The Historie of the World […], London:  […]  William Stansby for Walter Burre, […], →OCLC, 1st book:
quote.text: There is no likelihood between pure light and black darkness,  […] or between righteousness and reprobation.
